{•}ByteQuest.

Your progress belongs to you.

Last updated November 13, 2026

What the app stores

When you practise as a guest, ByteQuest saves drafts, notes, problem completion, review dates, confidence ratings and practice history in your browser. If you sign in, it uses your Google account’s basic profile and email for identity and saves your learning progress in the project’s Supabase database.

Who can see it

Published problems and their practice tests are public. Drafts, notes and learning progress are scoped to your signed-in user account through database access policies. The project owner can administer the database. Unpublished problems are available to appointed library editors.

Where code runs

Your Java solution compiles and executes on your device through CheerpJ. Signed-in drafts can be saved as part of your progress. Practice test results and XP are personal learning records, rather than independently verified competition scores.

Services the app uses

GitHub Pages hosts the website. Supabase provides the database and authentication, and Google handles Google sign-in. The browser also loads the Java runtime from CheerpJ, the Supabase client from esm.sh, and fonts from Google Fonts. These services receive the network request information needed to provide their features.

Backups and signing out

Use Backup to export your progress without authentication tokens. Sign out ends this app’s session on the current device and keeps the account’s saved progress. Guest work is kept separate from account work unless you choose to import it. Clearing browser site data removes local copies and sign-in state; it does not delete cloud records.

Project owner

ByteQuest is maintained through its GitHub repository. Contact the project owner about access or removal of cloud records. Avoid posting private information in public issues.
